## 9 - Error Handler

Set this workflow as the **Error Workflow** on workflows 1 to 5 (Settings > Error Workflow inside each workflow).

### How the error text is sanitised (v5)

A **string** error message is preserved, then sanitised. Nothing is deleted by line — secret *values* are redacted in place, so ordinary technical errors such as `Unexpected token '<' ... is not valid JSON` survive intact and reach you in full.

Replaced with `[redacted]`: Telegram bot tokens and `/bot<token>` URLs; `Bearer`, `Basic` and `Digest` credentials; labelled assignments (`api_key=`, `password:`, `token=`, `client_secret=` and similar); and any run of 32 or more identifier characters. **Header credentials** (`authorization`, `proxy-authorization`, `www-authenticate`, `cookie`, `set-cookie`, `x-api-key`) are redacted **to the end of the line**, because the whole header value is sensitive.

A **non-string** payload is never traversed. Allowlist extraction reads only `message`, `description`, `name`, `code`, `status`, `statusCode`, `httpCode` and `type`, descending only into `error`, `cause` and `details`. Unknown fields — including `credentials`, `node`, `headers`, `context`, `request`, `response`, `config`, `body` and `data` — are never read and never reach the Events message. Arrays are summarised as type and length only, unless an element is directly an allowlisted error object. A payload with no safe field yields `[non-string error payload omitted; type=...]`.

The Telegram message is HTML-escaped and sent with an explicit `parse_mode: HTML`. The sanitised output stays bounded by the existing 500-character limit. **The Events field mappings are unchanged.**

The failing action is marked FAILED **when an action id was identified**, rather than left mid-flight — that is what makes a retry safe: the approval gate in workflow 4 will not send twice for the same action. When no action id is found, no action status is changed and the notice says so.

> This behaviour is **unit-proven and statically verified** (1213 assertions). It is **not runtime-proven** — no real error has yet flowed through the published code.
